token.title: GitHub token
token.hint: A personal access token (classic) with the “read:user”, “repo” and “read:org” permissions: it loads your public repositories (those of your organizations too) and your account with private contributions. Without “repo” private contributions are counted but not split by type; without “read:org” organizations with hidden membership are left out.
token.label: Personal access token

guide.1: GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → Tokens (classic) → Generate new token (classic).
guide.2: Tick the scopes read:user, repo and read:org; the expiration is up to you (the token has to be replaced when it runs out).
guide.3: Copy the token — GitHub shows it only once — and paste it here.

key.title: Coding time
key.hint: The secret API key from wakatime.com → Settings → Account. It is stored encrypted and used only to read your coding time.
key.label: Secret API key

guide.1: Install the WakaTime plugin in your editor (wakatime.com/plugins) and sign in: it starts counting the time by itself.
guide.2: Open wakatime.com → Settings → Account and copy the Secret API Key.
guide.3: Paste it here. The last week is copied at once, and the history grows from then on.

summary.emptyHint: The summary adds up your activity on every connected service: one calendar, one streak.
summary.calendarHint: A day counts what was done on GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket together

token.title: GitLab token (gitlab.com)
token.hint: A personal access token with the “read_api” and “read_user” scopes: it loads your account with its activity (private projects too) and your public projects with those of your groups.

guide.1: GitLab → your avatar → Edit profile → Access tokens → Add new token.
guide.2: Tick the scopes read_api and read_user; the expiration is up to you (GitLab allows a year at most — the token has to be replaced when it runs out).
guide.3: Copy the token — GitLab shows it only once — and paste it here.

token.title: Bitbucket: e-mail and API token
token.hint: Bitbucket signs in with the e-mail of your Atlassian account and an API token. It loads your repositories, and your commits and pull requests in them — the activity calendar is built from those.
token.label: API token

guide.1: Atlassian account → Security → API tokens → Create API token with scopes.
guide.2: Choose the app Bitbucket and tick the read scopes: account, workspace, repository and pull request.
guide.3: Copy the token — it is shown only once.
guide.4: Enter here the e-mail you sign in to Atlassian with and the token.
